name: Use of English
subtitle: Second set in the same format: task 1 as matching from a word box, task 2 as multiple choice in a running text.
sourceNote: Our own practice in the style of the cloze tasks of Cambridge B2 First, Reading and Use of English. The word box and the three-option format are our adaptation, not the real paper's format. Texts and tasks are our own, not exam tasks.

exercises.title: Use of English, task 1 — Blog post: my phone stays in the kitchen
exercises.hint: Which word from the box fits which gap? Each word fits only once; two words are left over.

segments.text: For years, I charged my phone next to my bed and checked it last thing at night. My sleep,
had never been great, got even worse. By the time I finally decided to change my habits, I

been scrolling in the dark for at least two hours every night.

My solution was
a simple one that I wish I had tried it earlier: I bought an alarm clock and left my phone charging in the kitchen. At first I found it hard, but I fell asleep much faster

I had got used to the idea.

Now I have
intention of going back. If you had told me a year ago that I

be waking up before my alarm, I would never have believed you.

If you want to try the same thing, you can
buy an alarm clock or use an old watch with an alarm. Some people prefer to keep their phone within reach,
others find that even seeing it on the bedside table makes them want to pick it up. Whichever you choose, give it a week.
